prompt: Which statement gives the scientific definition of resultant force in Cambridge International AS Level Physics?
options: the rate of change of momentum of a body
the product of the mass and acceleration of a body
the energy transferred per unit distance
the product of mass and rate of change of speed

answer.explanation: Resultant force is fundamentally defined as the rate of change of momentum of a body.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. Newton's second law fundamentally defines force as the rate of change of momentum (F = Delta p / Delta t).
Option 2 gives F = ma, which is a special case valid only when mass is constant, not the universal definition.
Option 3 describes work per unit distance.
Option 4 omits direction by using speed instead of velocity.
hints: Recall the universal form of Newton's second law.
What quantity changes when a resultant force acts on a body over a time interval?
solution: Resultant force is defined as the rate of change of momentum of a body. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Warn students that while F = ma is common, Cambridge mark schemes specifically require 'rate of change of momentum' when asked for the definition of force.
Explain that this definition remains valid even when mass changes (e.g. rockets, water jets).
